headline: Media, gaming, publishing and education firms show mixed performance with varied IT spending signals.
summary: Revenue growth is uneven across sectors. Media giants report strong top‑line gains but also cost‑cutting pressure. Gaming shows both profit loss and high growth in digital revenue. Publishing and education see AI investments alongside earnings misses and layoffs.

industries.summary: Disney posted 8% revenue growth and a 43% jump in operating income, while WBD/Skydance and Versant posted modest or declining margins. Cost‑cutting dominates the agenda, with $3 bn savings targeted at Disney and $6 bn cuts at WBD/Skydance. Some firms, like Versant, are expanding digital platforms.

laggards.why: Revenue grew only 5% YoY and operating margin fell to 5.2%

themes.title: Cost‑cutting
themes.detail: Multiple firms announced multi‑billion dollar savings programs and layoffs.

themes.title: Digital platform expansion
themes.detail: Versant added FAST channels and new streaming memberships.

themes.title: AI & tech pilots
themes.detail: Disney’s CEO highlighted AI use in parks and future tech initiatives.

industries.it_note: IT spend is tightening at Disney and WBD/Skydance, but expanding at Versant and Cox.

industries.summary: Caesars posted record revenue but widened its net loss. Bally's saw strong revenue growth and is expanding technology. Light & Wonder and Brightstar focus on cost reduction and product innovation.

leaders.why: Revenue up 21.7% YoY and expanding tech investments

laggards.why: Widened GAAP net loss despite revenue growth

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
themes.detail: Bally's and Caesars reported double‑digit digital revenue increases.

themes.title: Cost‑reduction focus
themes.detail: Light & Wonder prioritises debt reduction; Caesars emphasizes AI will not replace face‑to‑face meetings.

themes.title: Product innovation
themes.detail: Brightstar launched next‑gen lottery solutions and a new Cash Pop game.

industries.it_note: IT spend is tightening at Caesars and Light & Wonder, while Bally's is expanding its digital platform.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer expands AI tools across Europe. Scholastic missed revenue targets and posted a large operating loss. Pearson shows accelerated growth and AI‑driven product launches.

leaders.why: Accelerated revenue growth and AI‑powered platform rollout

laggards.why: Revenue miss and widening operating loss

themes.title: AI expansion
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer and Pearson are adding AI capabilities to legal, tax and language products.

themes.title: Revenue pressure
themes.detail: Scholastic reported a $216.8 m revenue miss and a -42.5% operating margin.

industries.it_note: Both Wolters Kluwer and Pearson signal expanding IT spend on AI and digital platforms.
